components.note: 木 (wood) — 极 originally named the ridgepole, the highest beam of a roof, extended to 'extreme, utmost.'
及 (jí) gives the sound — 极 is also pronounced jí, an exact match.

其 was originally a pictograph of a winnowing basket, woven from bamboo strips and shown with a stand beneath it. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write the pronoun 'its, that,' and the basket sense was replaced by 箕.

example.hanzi: 这次考试的题目极其简单。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì de tímù jíqí jiǎndān.
example.english: The questions on this exam were extremely simple.
example.fact: The Mariana Trench's Challenger Deep is the deepest known point in Earth's oceans, plunging to roughly 10,935 meters — deep enough to submerge Mount Everest with more than two kilometers to spare. Only a handful of crewed vehicles have ever reached the bottom, and the pressure there is over 1,000 times that at sea level.

meanings: respectful form of address for older men

components.note: 帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'
Person — represents someone who teaches.
Suggests spreading knowledge, related to instructing others.

example.hanzi: 王师傅修车修了三十年了。
example.pinyin: Wáng shīfu xiū chē xiū le sānshí nián le.
example.english: Master Wang has been fixing cars for thirty years.
example.fact: Japanese sushi masters traditionally spend years on preparatory tasks — washing rice, wringing towels, and cooking rice properly — before a mentor lets them touch raw fish, a training path popularized internationally by the documentary Jiro Dreams of Sushi. The apprenticeship model reflects a broader craft tradition where mastery is earned gradually rather than taught directly.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — relates directly to 线's meaning 'line, thread, wire.'
戋 (jiān) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from xiàn.
足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.

example.hanzi: 这条线路每天都很堵。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiànlù měitiān dōu hěn dǔ.
example.english: This route is congested every day.
example.fact: The London Underground's Circle line, opened in 1884, was the world's first underground railway to form a complete loop, and early trains were pulled by steam locomotives that vented smoke into the tunnels — passengers reportedly grew accustomed to breathing sulphurous air on their commute.

components.note: 禾 (a grain plant) — a sweet-smelling crop
日 — here standing in for sweetness (originally 甘), giving the sense of a pleasant smell
⺼ (flesh) — intestines are a body organ.
昜 (yáng in related characters) gives a sound distantly related to cháng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 冰箱里还有几根香肠。
example.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ hái yǒu jǐ gēn xiāngcháng.
example.english: There are still a few sausages in the fridge.
example.fact: Sausages are one of the oldest processed foods on record — a Sumerian clay tablet from around 3000 BC already describes meat stuffed into animal intestine casings, a preservation method that let herders store protein long before refrigeration existed.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拖 describes pulling or dragging something by hand.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 他用皮卡拖车把船拖到了湖边。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng píkǎ tuōchē bǎ chuán tuō dào le hú biān.
example.english: He used his pickup truck's tow trailer to haul the boat to the lake.
example.fact: The Bagger 293, a bucket-wheel excavator used in German coal mining, is among the largest land vehicles ever built — about 220 meters long and 96 meters tall — and moves at a walking pace of roughly 10 meters per minute while stripping away hundreds of thousands of tons of earth per day.

components.note: 木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.
木 (wood) shows 械 relates to a wooden tool or device, extended to "equipment."
戒 (jiè) gives a sound close to xiè, differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 这台机械看起来非常复杂。
example.pinyin: Zhè tái jīxiè kànqǐlái fēicháng fùzá.
example.english: This machine looks extremely complicated.
example.fact: The Antikythera mechanism, recovered from a Greek shipwreck in 1901, is a hand-cranked bronze device built around 150-100 BC that could predict eclipses and track the positions of the sun, moon, and planets — historians consider it the world's oldest known analog computer.

components.note: 丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
乐 is the simplified form of 樂, which depicted a wooden 木 instrument strung with strings 幺, played with a pick 白 — music came to represent joy, giving 乐 its meaning 'happy, music.'

example.hanzi: 他每天午饭都要喝一杯可乐。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān wǔfàn dōu yào hē yì bēi kělè.
example.english: He drinks a glass of cola with lunch every day.
example.fact: Coca-Cola's original 1886 formula was invented by pharmacist John Pemberton as a patent medicine and, unusually for the era, contained coca leaf extract — a legal ingredient at the time — which the company removed from its recipe around 1903 as attitudes toward the substance shifted.

components.note: 八 (a hand shape) — one of two hands shown reaching toward the same object.
廾 (two hands together) — jointly holding up one object, giving 共 its meaning 'together, joint, common.'
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.

example.hanzi: 我们决定一起共度周末。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen juédìng yìqǐ gòngdù zhōumò.
example.english: We decided to spend the weekend together.
example.fact: Emperor penguins are famous for their extreme cooperative behavior in Antarctica's winter, huddling in tight rotating clusters of thousands of birds to share body heat while temperatures drop below minus 40 degrees Celsius — individuals on the windward edge periodically shuffle toward the warm center so no single bird bears the cold too long.

components.note: 纟 (silk/thread) — early paper was made from silk and plant fibers, linking 纸 to the thread radical.
氏 (shì) gives a sound distantly related to zhǐ, having drifted apart over time.
木 (tree, wood) — the traditional form 條 relates 条 to a slender branch or twig, extended to mean a long thin strip or an item in a list.
The upper strokes are a simplification of 攸 (yōu), which supplied a sound distantly related to tiáo, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 她在门上留了一张纸条。
example.pinyin: Tā zài mén shàng liú le yì zhāng zhǐtiáo.
example.english: She left a note on the door.
example.fact: The Post-it Note was born from a failed adhesive: 3M scientist Spencer Silver created a glue in 1968 that stuck to surfaces but peeled away cleanly, and it took another colleague, Art Fry, several years to realize it was perfect for bookmarks that wouldn't damage the page.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 污 describes water, or anything else, that has become dirty or polluted.
亏 (kuī) is only distantly related in sound to wū — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.
木 (wood) pictures a wooden dyeing vat.
氿-shaped strokes above picture liquid dye poured into it, giving 染 its meaning 'to dye.'

example.hanzi: 工厂排放的废水造成了严重污染。
example.pinyin: Gōngchǎng páifàng de fèishuǐ zàochéng le yánzhòng wūrǎn.
example.english: The wastewater discharged by the factory caused severe pollution.
example.fact: The Cuyahoga River in Cleveland caught fire at least a dozen times between the 1860s and 1969 due to industrial pollution and oil slicks on its surface, and the widely publicized 1969 fire helped spur the creation of the US Environmental Protection Agency the following year.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拘 describes physically restraining or seizing someone.
句 (jù) gives a sound close to jū, sharing the same rhyme.
田 (field) — 留 pictures someone stopping to work or rest on a plot of land.
The strokes above 田 are a simplification of 丣, once used mainly for its sound; together the character came to mean 'to remain, to stay, to keep.'

example.hanzi: 警方将嫌疑人拘留了二十四小时。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng jiāng xiányírén jūliú le èrshísì xiǎoshí.
example.english: The police detained the suspect for twenty-four hours.
example.fact: Alcatraz, the notorious island prison in San Francisco Bay, operated as a federal penitentiary from 1934 to 1963 and was chosen partly because the bay's cold currents and strong tides made escape by swimming extremely dangerous, though several inmates still attempted it.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 决 originally described water breaching a dike and bursting free, an image later extended to mean 'to decide, to resolve.'
The right-hand side is a simplification of 夬 (guài), which supplied a sound close to jué, differing mainly in the initial consonant.
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 他下定决心要学好英语。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàdìng juéxīn yào xuéhǎo Yīngyǔ.
example.english: He made up his mind to learn English well.
example.fact: Roald Amundsen's team beat Robert Falcon Scott's to the South Pole in 1911 partly through sheer resolve in preparation: Amundsen had spent years studying Inuit survival techniques and relied on sled dogs, while Scott's expedition used motor sledges and ponies that struggled badly in the polar conditions.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 坚 relates to solid, packed ground, the source of its meaning 'firm, solid, resolute.'
The upper part is a simplification of 臤, which pictured a hand gripping something tightly — a grip firm enough to hold fast, reinforcing the sense of 'firm.'
亻 (person) — pairs with 言 to depict a person's spoken word.
言 (speech) — a person's words that can be trusted gave 信 its meaning 'to believe, to trust,' and later 'letter, message.'

example.hanzi: 我坚信努力一定会有回报。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jiānxìn nǔlì yídìng huì yǒu huíbào.
example.english: I firmly believe that hard work will pay off.
example.fact: Ignaz Semmelweis, a 19th-century Hungarian physician, firmly believed that unwashed hands were spreading fatal infections in maternity wards, and after he required doctors to wash with a chlorinated solution, mortality rates dropped sharply — yet his peers largely dismissed the idea, and it wasn't widely accepted until decades after his death.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刹 relates to cutting off, stopping.
杀 (shā) gives the sound — an exact match with 刹.
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 司机猛地刹车,车上的人都晃了一下。
example.pinyin: Sījī měngde shāchē, chē shàng de rén dōu huàng le yíxià.
example.english: The driver slammed on the brakes, and everyone in the car lurched.
example.fact: Antilock braking systems (ABS), now standard on most cars, were first developed for aircraft in the 1950s to prevent wheels from locking up on landing, and the technology only migrated to passenger vehicles in the 1970s once electronic sensors became cheap and reliable enough.

components.note: 人 (person), doubled — one person shown following another depicts the idea of accompanying or coming from somewhere.
事 was originally a pictograph of a hand holding a forked tally stick or hunting tool used by an official on duty, giving the character its meaning 'affair, matter, to serve, to attend to.'

example.hanzi: 他大学毕业后一直从事教育工作。
example.pinyin: Tā dàxué bìyè hòu yìzhí cóngshì jiàoyù gōngzuò.
example.english: Since graduating from university, he has worked in education.
example.fact: Before becoming a full-time author, Stan Lee spent years writing comics for what was then Timely Comics under various pseudonyms, and it wasn't until 1961, with the launch of the Fantastic Four, that he and artist Jack Kirby began building the shared universe that became Marvel Comics.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 位 relates to a person's location.
立 (to stand) — the spot where a person stands gave 位 its meaning 'position' or 'place,' and later, a polite measure word for people.

于's ancient form pictured breath curling up and out of a narrow opening, an image of something being emitted or extended outward. The character was later borrowed almost entirely for its sound to serve as the grammatical particle 'at, in, from.'

example.hanzi: 这座图书馆位于市中心。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò túshūguǎn wèiyú shì zhōngxīn.
example.english: This library is located in the city center.
example.fact: The Library of Alexandria, founded in Egypt around the 3rd century BC, is estimated to have held several hundred thousand papyrus scrolls at its peak and employed scholars tasked with collecting a copy of every known text in the ancient world — its eventual loss remains one of history's most-cited cultural tragedies, though the exact cause is still debated.

components.note: 马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.
又 (hand) shows a hand performing an action.
戈 (spear) — mock combat and stage tricks with weapons gave 戏 its meaning 'play, drama.'
才 (talent) — many talented people.
囗 (an enclosure) — gathered together in one place, giving 团 its meaning 'group, team; round, ball-shaped.'

example.hanzi: 孩子们都很期待马戏团的表演。
example.pinyin: Háizimen dōu hěn qídài mǎxìtuán de biǎoyǎn.
example.english: The children are all looking forward to the circus performance.
example.fact: Ringling Bros. and Barnum & Bailey Circus, once billed as 'The Greatest Show on Earth,' operated continuously from 1871 until it closed in 2017 after 146 years, a shutdown driven partly by declining ticket sales following its 2016 decision to retire its famous elephant acts.

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
扌 (hand) — the hand doing the sowing.
番 (a field marked out into plots) — seeds scattered by hand across it, giving 播 its meaning 'to sow, to spread, to broadcast.'

example.hanzi: 这个消息很快就在网上传播开了。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi hěn kuài jiù zài wǎngshàng chuánbō kāi le.
example.english: This news quickly spread online.
example.fact: The 1918 influenza pandemic is estimated to have infected roughly a third of the world's population and killed at least 50 million people, spreading rapidly along the troop movements and crowded conditions of the final months of World War I — a pattern epidemiologists still study when modeling how diseases travel through connected populations.

components.note: 母 (mǔ, 'mother') serves as the phonetic base; the sound has since diverged from měi, so the connection is mostly historical today.
The upper part is a simplification of 尚, once used mainly for its sound and a sense of 'esteem, correspondence.'

The lower part is a simplification of 田 (field) from the traditional form 當, which compared two fields of matching value — giving 当 its meaning 'to correspond to, to be equivalent to; when, at the time of.'

example.hanzi: 每当下雨,他就会想起家乡。
example.pinyin: Měidāng xiàyǔ, tā jiù huì xiǎngqǐ jiāxiāng.
example.english: Whenever it rains, he thinks of his hometown.
example.fact: Petrichor, the distinctive earthy smell after rain, comes partly from geosmin, a compound produced by soil-dwelling bacteria called actinomycetes — human noses are remarkably sensitive to it, able to detect concentrations as low as a few parts per trillion.

components.note: The upper part, related to 土, traditionally depicted one person's fate.
干 depicted a contrasting fate — the character set two outcomes side by side, with the fortunate one giving 幸 its meaning 'lucky, fortunate.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 幸好他带了雨伞,不然就淋湿了。
example.pinyin: Xìnghǎo tā dài le yǔsǎn, bùrán jiù línshī le.
example.english: Luckily he brought an umbrella, or he would have gotten soaked.
example.fact: In 1943, engineer Richard James accidentally invented the Slinky when a torsion spring he was developing to stabilize ship equipment fell off a shelf and 'walked' across the floor instead of just clattering down — a lucky mishap that became one of the best-selling toys of the 20th century.

components.note: 戈 (a blade) — 裁 involves cutting.
衣 (clothing) — cutting cloth to make or trim clothing, giving 裁 its meaning 'to cut out, to reduce.'
刂 (knife) — 判 originally related to cutting something apart to distinguish or decide
半 (bàn) gives a sound close to 判's reading pàn, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 裁判判他犯规,取消了这个球。
example.pinyin: Cáipàn pàn tā fànguī, qǔxiāo le zhège qiú.
example.english: The referee ruled it a foul and disallowed the goal.
example.fact: Goal-line technology in soccer, which uses multiple high-speed cameras to determine within millimeters whether a ball has fully crossed the line, was first used at a major tournament in the 2014 World Cup — a response to decades of contested goals that referees on the pitch simply couldn't see clearly enough.

components.note: 冏 (bright, a window admitting light) — appears in 商's ancient form, though its exact link to 'commerce, to discuss' is unclear today.
章 — a graphic element whose original contribution to the character's meaning has been lost over time.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 他是当地很有名的商人。
example.pinyin: Tā shì dāngdì hěn yǒumíng de shāngrén.
example.english: He is a well-known businessman in the local area.
example.fact: The Medici family rose from relatively modest origins in 14th-century Florence to become one of Europe's most powerful banking dynasties, and their wealth from trade and finance directly funded much of the early Italian Renaissance, including commissions to artists like Michelangelo and Botticelli.

components.note: A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
⺼ (flesh/body) — 胆 names a body organ, the gallbladder.
旦 (dàn) gives a sound close to dǎn, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 他竟然大胆地在会上提出反对意见。
example.pinyin: Tā jìngrán dàdǎn de zài huì shàng tíchū fǎnduì yìjiàn.
example.english: He boldly raised his objection in the meeting.
example.fact: In 1911, art thief Vincenzo Peruggia walked out of the Louvre with the Mona Lisa hidden under his coat during regular opening hours, simply by hiding overnight in a supply closet — the painting was missing for over two years before he was caught trying to sell it in Italy.

components.note: Bird — an older semantic root kept from an earlier character shape.
Gives the sound hù, related to gù but drifted apart over time.

用 is generally thought to depict a wooden bucket or a fenced-in pen viewed from the side, though scholars disagree on the exact original object. The character was extended from naming a useful container to meaning 'to use, to employ.'

example.hanzi: 这家公司准备雇用十名新员工。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhǔnbèi gùyòng shí míng xīn yuángōng.
example.english: This company is planning to hire ten new employees.
example.fact: The Ford Motor Company's decision in 1914 to pay assembly-line workers five dollars a day — roughly double the prevailing wage — was initially seen as reckless by other industrialists, but it sharply cut worker turnover and let employees afford the very cars they were building.

components.note: 欠 (breath, an open mouth exhaling) — 歌 relates to the breath used in singing.
哥 (gē) gives the sound — an exact match with 歌's reading gē.
口 (mouth) — 唱 describes singing, an action made with the mouth.
昌 (chāng) gives a sound close to chàng, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 孩子们围在一起歌唱。
example.pinyin: Háizimen wéi zài yìqǐ gēchàng.
example.english: The children gathered together and sang.
example.fact: Humpback whale songs, which can last up to 30 minutes and repeat in structured phrases, are thought to spread between populations like cultural trends — researchers have tracked entirely new songs originating off Australia and spreading eastward across the Pacific over several years.

components.note: 鬲 (an ancient three-legged cauldron) — 融 originally described steam rising from a cooking pot as it heated, i.e. melting or blending.
虫 (chóng) gives a sound distantly related to róng, having drifted apart over time.
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.hanzi: 新来的同事很快就融入了团队。
example.pinyin: Xīn lái de tóngshì hěn kuài jiù róngrù le tuánduì.
example.english: The new colleague quickly integrated into the team.
example.fact: Coral reefs form through a close partnership between coral polyps and microscopic algae called zooxanthellae, which live inside the coral's tissue and photosynthesize sunlight into food; when ocean temperatures rise, corals expel these algae in a stress response known as bleaching, often leading to reef death.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — the living thing in bloom.
化 (transformation) — the plant changing into blossom, the source of 花's meaning 'flower.'
钅 (metal) — 钱 relates to money, since early Chinese coins were made of metal
戋 (jiān) gives a loose sound connection to 钱's reading qián

example.hanzi: 他一到周末就喜欢出去花钱。
example.pinyin: Tā yí dào zhōumò jiù xǐhuān chūqù huāqián.
example.english: As soon as the weekend arrives, he likes to go out and spend money.
example.fact: Lydia, an ancient kingdom in what is now western Turkey, is generally credited with minting the world's first standardized metal coins around the 7th century BC, made from electrum, a naturally occurring alloy of gold and silver.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 避 means to avoid, moving away from something.
辟 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 避.
廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'

example.hanzi: 他绕了远路,想避开堵车。
example.pinyin: Tā rào le yuǎnlù, xiǎng bìkāi dǔchē.
example.english: He took a longer route to avoid the traffic jam.
example.fact: Migratory birds such as bar-tailed godwits can detect approaching storms through changes in barometric pressure and will delay or reroute multi-thousand-kilometer flights to avoid flying directly into severe weather over open ocean, where there is nowhere to land and rest.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) shows the movement of making rounds.
巛 (a flowing river shape) suggests a winding route being walked, giving 巡 its meaning 'to patrol, to make one's rounds.'
辶 (to walk) shows 逻 relates to movement, as in patrolling on foot.
罗 (luó) gives the exact sound of 逻.

example.hanzi: 警察每晚都会在这条街上巡逻。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá měi wǎn dōu huì zài zhè tiáo jiē shàng xúnluó.
example.english: Police patrol this street every night.
example.fact: The Great Wall of China was never a single continuous structure but a network of walls, watchtowers, and beacon towers built and rebuilt by different dynasties over roughly two thousand years, and Ming-era garrisons used smoke and fire signals from tower to tower to relay warnings of approaching threats faster than any rider could travel.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'
八 (to divide/split) — represents something being separated into smaller parts.
亅 (a hook/line) — cutting a small piece off, an image tied to the meaning 'small, tiny.'

example.hanzi: 花园角落里有一片小小的菜地。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán jiǎoluò lǐ yǒu yí piàn xiǎoxiǎo de càidì.
example.english: There's a tiny vegetable patch in the corner of the garden.
example.fact: Tardigrades, microscopic animals often called 'water bears,' can survive in a dried-out state for over a decade and endure conditions that would kill nearly any other animal, including the vacuum of space — several species were sent into low Earth orbit in 2007 and survived direct solar radiation exposure.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 吸 describes breathing in through the mouth.
及 (jí) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading xī has diverged.
火 (fire) — smoke, 烟's meaning, rises from fire.
因 (yīn) gives a rhyme close to yān, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 医院里到处都写着禁止吸烟。
example.pinyin: Yīyuàn lǐ dàochù dōu xiězhe jìnzhǐ xīyān.
example.english: Signs banning smoking are posted everywhere in the hospital.
example.fact: The link between smoking and lung cancer was firmly established by large epidemiological studies in the early 1950s, notably by Richard Doll and Austin Bradford Hill in the UK, whose research tracking thousands of British doctors provided some of the first solid statistical evidence connecting the habit to the disease.

components.note: 八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
衣 (cloth) — 裂 describes cloth tearing apart.
列 (liè) is an exact match for the sound of 裂.

example.hanzi: 这个组织内部出现了严重分裂。
example.pinyin: Zhège zǔzhī nèibù chūxiàn le yánzhòng fēnliè.
example.english: A serious split emerged within this organization.
example.fact: Nuclear fission, the splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus into smaller fragments, was first experimentally demonstrated in 1938 by Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann, with Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch providing the theoretical explanation shortly after — a discovery that release enormous energy and set the stage for both nuclear power and nuclear weapons.

meanings: notebook (abbr. for 筆記本電腦|笔记本电脑[bi3 ji4 ben3 dian4 nao3])

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) depicts the shaft of a writing brush.
毛 (hair) depicts the bristled tip of the brush — together giving 笔 its meaning 'writing brush, pen.'
讠 (speech/writing) — the act of putting words down.
己 (oneself, private) — writing down one's own private notes or memories, giving 记 its meaning 'to record, remember.'
木 (tree) — provides the base image of a tree.
一 (a line) marks the base of the trunk, highlighting the roots — giving 本 its meaning 'root, origin, source.'

example.hanzi: 他把资料存在了笔记本电脑里。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ zīliào cún zài le bǐjìběn diànnǎo lǐ.
example.english: He saved the files on his laptop.
example.fact: The first commercially successful laptop, the Osborne 1, was released in 1981, weighed about 11 kilograms, and had a screen barely five inches wide — yet it was considered revolutionary for being 'portable' at all, since most computers at the time filled entire rooms or desks.

components.note: 禾 (a grain plant) — a sweet-smelling crop
日 — here standing in for sweetness (originally 甘), giving the sense of a pleasant smell
艹 (grass, plant) — 蕉 (the banana plant) is a plant.
焦 (jiāo) gives the sound — an exact match with 蕉's reading.

example.hanzi: 猴子最爱吃的水果就是香蕉。
example.pinyin: Hóuzi zuì ài chī de shuǐguǒ jiùshì xiāngjiāo.
example.english: The fruit monkeys love most is bananas.
example.fact: Nearly all commercially grown bananas belong to a single cultivar called the Cavendish, propagated by cloning rather than seed, which makes the entire global supply genetically identical and highly vulnerable to disease — a fungal outbreak called Panama disease has already wiped out the previous dominant variety, the Gros Michel, in the mid-20th century.

components.note: 冖 here is a distorted form of 力 (strength) — a simplified way of showing soldiers grouped together.
车 (cart/vehicle) — 军 originally pictured soldiers riding out to battle in war chariots.
宀 (roof) — 官 relates to a building associated with public duty, such as a government office.
吕 depicts a stacked, mound-like shape thought to represent an early military garrison under a roof; the sense of a post of authority later narrowed to mean 'government official.'

example.hanzi: 他是一位受人尊敬的军官。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi shòu rén zūnjìng de jūnguān.
example.english: He is a well-respected military officer.
example.fact: The Enigma machine used by German military officers in World War II was considered virtually unbreakable, yet a team at Bletchley Park led by mathematicians including Alan Turing built machines called 'bombes' that could crack its daily settings, an intelligence breakthrough historians credit with shortening the war significantly.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person shown advancing on something.
The remaining strokes are a worn-down picture of a hand holding a broom, sweeping steadily forward — an image of gradual, creeping advance that gave 侵 its meaning 'to invade, to encroach upon.'
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.hanzi: 敌军趁夜色侵入了边境村庄。
example.pinyin: Díjūn chèn yèsè qīnrù le biānjìng cūnzhuāng.
example.english: The enemy troops invaded the border village under cover of darkness.
example.fact: Cane toads were deliberately introduced to Australia in 1935 to control beetles damaging sugarcane crops, but the toads failed to eat the target pest and instead spread explosively across the continent, becoming one of the most notorious invasive species in modern ecological history.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伏 describes a person's posture, crouched low to the ground.
犬 (dog) — paired with the person 亻, the image of someone lying low like a dog gave 伏 its meaning 'to crouch, to lie hidden.'
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 这个灯泡需要220伏特的电压。
example.pinyin: Zhège dēngpào xūyào èrbǎi'èrshí fútè de diànyā.
example.english: This light bulb requires a voltage of 220 volts.
example.fact: The volt is named after Alessandro Volta, the Italian physicist who invented the first true battery, the voltaic pile, in 1800 by stacking alternating discs of zinc and copper separated by brine-soaked cloth — the first device able to produce a steady, continuous electric current.

components.note: 马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.
木 (wood) — 桶 names an object often made of wood, a bucket.
甬 (yǒng) gives a sound only distantly related to tǒng today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 旧房子里还留着一个老式马桶。
example.pinyin: Jiù fángzi lǐ hái liú zhe yí gè lǎoshì mǎtǒng.
example.english: There's still an old-fashioned chamber pot left in the old house.
example.fact: Sir John Harington, godson of Queen Elizabeth I, designed an early flush toilet in 1596 and installed one for the queen at Richmond Palace, but the invention was largely ignored for nearly two centuries until Alexander Cumming patented an improved flush design in 1775.

components.note: 少 depicts a few small dots or grains, like scattered sand — a simple picture of a small quantity, giving the meaning 'few' or 'little.'
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'

example.hanzi: 他从少年时期就开始学习画画。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng shàonián shíqī jiù kāishǐ xuéxí huàhuà.
example.english: He started learning to paint from his teenage years.
example.fact: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart began composing music at the age of five and was touring European royal courts as a performing prodigy by age six, with his father chronicling and promoting his early talent across years of demanding travel.

components.note: 口 depicts a mouth.
喿 depicts three mouths in a tree, representing birds chirping — paired with another mouth, the image is one of noisy chatter, giving 噪 its meaning 'noisy.'
立 here depicts a tongue positioned to speak.
日 here depicts an open mouth — a tongue forming sound in the mouth gave 音 its meaning 'sound, tone.'

example.hanzi: 工地传来的噪音吵得人睡不着。
example.pinyin: Gōngdì chuánlái de zàoyīn chǎo de rén shuìbùzháo.
example.english: The noise from the construction site was so loud that people couldn't sleep.
example.fact: Sound is measured on a logarithmic decibel scale, meaning every increase of 10 decibels represents a tenfold increase in sound intensity — a jet engine at close range, around 140 decibels, is roughly ten trillion times more intense than the quietest sound the human ear can detect.

meanings: the only son of a family

components.note: 单 is the simplified form of 單, an ancient pictograph of a forked hunting weapon topped with a net or pouch for hurling stones — unrelated to its current meaning. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write 'single, sole, one.'
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 他是家里的单子,爷爷奶奶特别宠他。
example.pinyin: Tā shì jiā lǐ de dānzǐ, yéye nǎinai tèbié chǒng tā.
example.english: He is the only son in the family, and his grandparents dote on him especially.
example.fact: China's one-child policy, enforced from 1980 to 2015, led to a generation sometimes called 'little emperors' — only children who, without siblings, often received concentrated parental and grandparental attention and resources, a demographic shift sociologists are still studying decades later.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 把 relates to grasping or holding something with the hand.
巴 (bā) gives the sound — 把 is pronounced bǎ, a close match differing only in tone.
又 (hand) shows a hand performing an action.
戈 (spear) — mock combat and stage tricks with weapons gave 戏 its meaning 'play, drama.'

example.hanzi: 这只是魔术师的把戏,别被骗了。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǐshì móshùshī de bǎxì, bié bèi piàn le.
example.english: This is just the magician's trick, don't be fooled.
example.fact: Harry Houdini, one of history's most famous escape artists, died in 1926 not from a failed stunt but from a ruptured appendix, after a college student punched him in the stomach backstage to test a claim that Houdini could withstand any blow — he continued performing for days before the injury proved fatal.

components.note: 夂 (a foot, to walk) — 各 pictures people arriving from different directions.
口 (mouth) — different people speaking gave 各 its meaning 'each' or 'every,' emphasizing individual distinctness.
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

example.hanzi: 这种植物在各地都能生长。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng zhíwù zài gèdì dōu néng shēngzhǎng.
example.english: This kind of plant can grow in all sorts of places.
example.fact: Dandelions are found on every continent except Antarctica and can reproduce through a process called apomixis, producing viable seeds without needing pollination at all — a trait that has helped the plant spread into an astonishing range of climates and soil types worldwide.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 迎 describes walking out to meet and welcome someone.
卬 (áng) gives a sound distantly related to yíng, having drifted apart over time.
扌 (hand) — 接 relates to receiving or connecting something by hand.
妾 (qiè) gives a hint of the sound — 接 is pronounced jiē, a connection that has shifted over time.

example.hanzi: 全家人都到机场迎接他回国。
example.pinyin: Quán jiā rén dōu dào jīchǎng yíngjiē tā huíguó.
example.english: The whole family went to the airport to welcome him home.
example.fact: When the Apollo 11 astronauts returned to Earth in 1969, they were quarantined for 21 days before their public welcome, as NASA — with no way to be sure moon dust was safe — took the precaution of isolating the crew in case they had brought back any unknown lunar microorganisms.

components.note: 手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 他手头现在有点紧,想借点钱。
example.pinyin: Tā shǒutóu xiànzài yǒudiǎn jǐn, xiǎng jiè diǎn qián.
example.english: He's a bit short on cash right now and wants to borrow some money.
example.fact: Before paper money existed, several ancient societies used commodity currencies with intrinsic value, including cacao beans in Mesoamerica and salt in parts of Africa and Rome — the word 'salary' itself is often traced to the Latin word for salt, reflecting how directly people once linked pay to physical goods.

components.note: 大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
疒 (sickness) — 痛 relates to physical pain or illness
甬 (yǒng) gives a sound distantly related to 痛's reading tòng, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 他昨天喝多了酒,今天头痛得厉害。
example.pinyin: Tā zuótiān hē duō le jiǔ, jīntiān tóutòng de lìhài.
example.english: He drank too much yesterday and has a terrible headache today.
example.fact: Migraines are increasingly understood to involve waves of altered electrical activity spreading across the brain's surface, called cortical spreading depression, which researchers believe can trigger the visual disturbances, known as auras, that some migraine sufferers experience before the pain even begins.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — 蝴 names a type of insect.
胡 (hú) gives the sound — an exact match with 蝴's reading.
虫 (insect) — 蝶 names an insect, the butterfly.
枼 (yè) gives a sound only distantly related to dié today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 花园里飞来了一只漂亮的蝴蝶。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ fēi lái le yì zhī piàoliang de húdié.
example.english: A beautiful butterfly flew into the garden.
example.fact: Monarch butterflies migrate up to 4,800 kilometers between Canada and central Mexico each year, yet no single butterfly completes the round trip — the journey takes multiple generations, with each one somehow inheriting the route information needed to continue it, a phenomenon still not fully understood by biologists.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — vomiting happens through the mouth.
区 (qū) gives a sound distantly related to 呕's reading ǒu, having drifted apart over time.
口 (mouth) shows 吐 relates to an action of the mouth.
土 (tǔ) gives the exact sound of 吐.

example.hanzi: 她晕车晕得厉害,一路都在呕吐。
example.pinyin: Tā yùnchē yùn de lìhài, yílù dōu zài ǒutù.
example.english: She got badly carsick and was vomiting the whole way.
example.fact: Motion sickness is thought to arise from a mismatch between what the inner ear senses about movement and what the eyes perceive, a conflict some scientists suspect the brain interprets as a possible sign of poisoning, triggering nausea as a defensive reflex.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'
⺷ (sheep, related to 羊) — 义 relates to what is right or moral, linked to the idea of sacrificial sheep used in rituals of righteousness.
乂 (yì) gives the sound — 义 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 这本词典对这个词的定义很清楚。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn cídiǎn duì zhège cí de dìngyì hěn qīngchǔ.
example.english: This dictionary's definition of the word is very clear.
example.fact: The Oxford English Dictionary's first edition took over 70 years to complete, from its initial planning in 1857 to its full publication in 1928, and relied heavily on thousands of volunteer readers who mailed in slips of paper citing how words were actually used in print.

components.note: 厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 反 pictures pushing against a steep surface.
又 (a hand) — a hand pushing back against a cliff gave 反 its meaning 'to turn over' or 'opposite.'
而 was originally a pictograph of a hanging beard or set of whiskers seen in profile. The character was later borrowed for its sound to serve as a grammatical connector meaning 'and, but, yet.'

example.hanzi: 他没有生气,反而笑了起来。
example.pinyin: Tā méiyǒu shēngqì, fǎn'ér xiào le qǐlái.
example.english: He wasn't angry — on the contrary, he started laughing.
example.fact: Placebo treatments in clinical trials sometimes produce real, measurable physiological effects even though the pills contain no active ingredient, an outcome researchers attribute partly to genuine changes in brain chemistry triggered by expectation — a phenomenon robust enough that trial designers must account for it when testing new drugs.
